'''MDPI''' ('''Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute''') is a [[publisher]] of open-access [[scientific journals]]. It publishes over 390 peer-reviewed, open-access journals.<ref name="UA">{{cite journal |last1=Fosso |first1=Olav Bjarte |author-link1=Olav Bjarte Fosso |last2=Nøland |first2=Jonas Kristiansen |date=6 January 2020 |title=Forskere blir ledet til etiske overtramp |trans-title=Researchers are led into ethical transgressions |url=https://www.universitetsavisa.no/ytring/forskere-blir-ledet-til-etiske-overtramp/114691 |journal=Universitetsavisa}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=MDPI {{!}} Journals A–Z|url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/journals|access-date=2022-02-25|website=www.mdpi.com}}</ref> MDPI is among the largest publishers in the world in terms of journal article output,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Petrou |first=Christos |date=2022-11-08 |title=Guest Post – Publishing Fast and Slow: A Review of Publishing Speed in the Last Decade |url=https://scholarlykitchen.sspnet.org/2022/11/08/guest-post-publishing-fast-and-slow-a-review-of-publishing-speed-in-the-last-decade/ |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=The Scholarly Kitchen |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Csomos">{{Cite journal |last1=Csomós |first1=György |last2=Farkas |first2=Jenő Zsolt |date=2022-11-14 |title=Understanding the increasing market share of the academic publisher "Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute" in the publication output of Central and Eastern European countries: a case study of Hungary |journal=Scientometrics |volume=128 |pages=803–824 |language=en |doi=10.1007/s11192-022-04586-1 |s2cid=253535738 |issn=1588-2861|doi-access=free }}</ref> and was the largest publisher of open access articles in 2020.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=10 August 2020|title=Guest Post – MDPI's Remarkable Growth|url=https://scholarlykitchen.sspnet.org/2020/08/10/guest-post-mdpis-remarkable-growth/|access-date=1 March 2021|website=The Scholarly Kitchen|language=en-US}}</ref>

It was founded by Shu-Kun Lin as a chemical sample archive.<ref name=":14">{{cite book |last=Lin |first=S.-K. |chapter=Chemical Samples Recycling: The MDPI Samples Preservation and Exchange Project |date=2005 |title=Environmental Chemistry |pages=585–590 |editor-last=Lichtfouse |editor-first=Eric |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/3-540-26531-7_53 |access-date=2024-02-07 |place=Berlin/Heidelberg |publisher=Springer-Verlag |language=en |doi=10.1007/3-540-26531-7_53 |isbn=978-3-540-22860-8 |editor2-last=Schwarzbauer |editor2-first=Jan |editor3-last=Robert |editor3-first=Didier}}</ref> Between 2016 and 2020, the number of peer-reviewed papers published by MDPI grew significantly, with year-over-year growth of over 50% in 2017, 2018 and 2019,<ref name=":0" /> attracting attention to their very fast article processing times.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Crosetto |first=Paolo |date=2021-04-12 |title=Is MDPI a predatory publisher? |url=https://paolocrosetto.wordpress.com/2021/04/12/is-mdpi-a-predatory-publisher/ |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=Paolo Crosetto's Blog |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite web |date=2023-03-15 |title=Quality questions as publisher's growth challenges big players |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/quality-questions-publishers-growth-challenges-big-players |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=Times Higher Education |language=en}}</ref> In a review of 26 open-access "mega-journals" that published over 3,500 papers in 2022, 11 (42%) of the journals were from MDPI.<ref name="mega-journals">{{cite journal |last1=Ioannidis |first1=John P. A. |last2=Pezzullo |first2=Angelo Maria |last3=Boccia |first3=Stefania |title=The Rapid Growth of Mega-Journals: Threats and Opportunities |journal=JAMA |date=20 March 2023 |volume=329 |issue=15 |pages=1253–1254 |doi=10.1001/jama.2023.3212|pmid=36939740 |s2cid=257630165 }}</ref> Besides launching its own journals, MDPI has acquired journals from other publishers, such as ''Tomography'' from Grapho Publications in 2021,<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.3390/tomography7010006 | doi-access=free | title=Publisher's Note: Continued Publication of Tomography by MDPI | date=2021 | last1=Vazquez | first1=Franck | journal=Tomography | volume=7 | issue=1 | page=65 | pmid=33704225 | pmc=8048370 }}</ref> and ''Nursing Reports''<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.3390/nursrep10010001 | doi-access=free | title=Publisher's Note: Continued Publication of Nursing Reports by MDPI | date=2020 | last1=Vazquez | first1=Franck | journal=Nursing Reports | volume=10 | issue=1 | page=1 | pmid=34968258 | pmc=8608059 }}</ref> and ''Audiology Research''<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.3390/audiolres10020008 | doi-access=free | title=Publisher's Note: Continued Publication of Audiology Research by MDPI | date=2020 | last1=Lin | first1=Shu-Kun | last2=Vicario | first2=Unai | last3=Vazquez | first3=Franck | journal=Audiology Research | volume=10 | issue=2 | page=49 | pmid=33093435 | pmc=7735433 }}</ref> from PagePress Publications in 2020.

As of January 2024, MDPI publishes 433 academic journals, including 92 journals indexed within the [[Science Citation Index Expanded]], 7 journals indexed within the [[Social Sciences Citation Index]],<ref>{{Cite web |publisher=Web of Science Group, a Clarivate company |title=Web of Science Master Journal List |url=https://mjl.clarivate.com/ |access-date=2023-07-25}}</ref> 138 journals listed in [[SciFinder]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scifinder-n.cas.org/search/reference/63e15d979eb0592f00dce02a/1|title=SciFinder® Login}}</ref> and 270 in [[Scopus]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/sources.uri|title=Scopus preview - Scopus - Sources|website=www.scopus.com}}</ref> Its journals are included in the [[Directory of Open Access Journals|DOAJ]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://doaj.org/|title=Directory of Open Access Journals|last=DOAJ|website=doaj.org|language=en|access-date=31 March 2020}}</ref> MDPI also publishes [[Open-access book|open access books]] indexed in [[DOAB]], [[OAPEN]] and [[Book Citation Index|BCI]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Information |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/information/indexing |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=www.mdpi.com |language=en}}</ref> It is a member of the [[Open Access Scholarly Publishing Association|Open Access Scholarly Publishers Association]] (OASPA),<ref>{{cite web |title=OASPA Members |url=https://oaspa.org/membership/members/ |access-date=1 September 2019}}</ref> the [[Committee on Publication Ethics]] (COPE),<ref>{{cite web |title=COPE: MDPI (Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute), 190 Member Journals |work=COPE: Committee on Publication Ethics |url=https://publicationethics.org/taxonomy/term/584/ |access-date=1 September 2019 |archive-date=1 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901052510/https://publicationethics.org/taxonomy/term/584/ }}</ref> the [[International Association of Scientific, Technical, and Medical Publishers]] (STM),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Members |url=https://www.stm-assoc.org/membership-2/our-members/ |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=STM |language=en-US}}</ref> and a participating publisher and supporter of the [[Initiative for Open Citations]] (I4OC).<ref>{{cite web |title=Initiative for Open Citations |url=https://i4oc.org/ |access-date=1 September 2019}}</ref>

MDPI's business model is based on establishing entirely open access broad-discipline journals, with fast processing times from submission to publication and [[article processing charge]]s paid by the author, their institutions or funders.<ref name=":0" /> MDPI's business practices have attracted controversy,<ref name="Vrieze" /><ref name="ASH2017">{{cite news |last=Pal |first=Shalmali |date=1 January 2017 |title=Predatory Publishing: The Dark Side of the Open-Access Movement |url=https://www.ashclinicalnews.org/features/predatory-publishing-dark-side-open-access-movement/ |work=ASH Clinical News}}</ref> with critics suggesting it sacrifices editorial and academic rigor in favor of operational speed and business interests.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=13 May 2020|title=There is no black and white definition of predatory publishing|url=https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/impactofsocialsciences/2020/05/13/there-is-no-black-and-white-definition-of-predatory-publishing/|access-date=5 March 2021|website=Impact of Social Sciences}}</ref> MDPI was included on [[Jeffrey Beall's list]] of [[predatory open access publishing]] companies in 2014;<ref name="Gillis">{{cite journal |last1=Gillis |first1=Alex |date=12 January 2017 |title=Beware! Academics are getting reeled in by scam journals |url=http://www.universityaffairs.ca/features/feature-article/beware-academics-getting-reeled-scam-journals/ |journal=University Affairs}}</ref><ref name="Beall2014" /> it was removed in 2015 following a successful appeal,<ref name="ASH2017" /><ref name="Gillis" /> while applying pressure on Beall's employer.<ref name="biochemia" /> Some journals published by MDPI have also been noted by the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS) and [[Norwegian Scientific Publication Register|Norwegian Scientific Index]] for lack of rigor and possible predatory practices;<ref name="Universitetsavisa2021">{{cite news |title=Plasserer tretten vitenskapelige tidsskrift på gråsone-nivå |work=Universitetsavisa |url=https://www.universitetsavisa.no/anne-kristine-borresen-publisering-uhr/plasserer-tretten-vitenskapelige-tidsskrift-pa-grasone-niva/198795 |access-date=7 September 2021}}</ref><ref name="khrono2021">{{cite web |date=27 May 2021 |title=Vi innfører nivå X for tvilsomme tidsskrifter |trans-title=We are introducing level X for dubious journals |url=https://khrono.no/vi-innforer-niva-x-for-tvilsomme-tidsskrifter/582556 |access-date=27 May 2021 |publisher=Khrono}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> as of 2025, CAS no longer lists any MDPI journals on its Early Warning List.<ref>{{Cite web |title=国际期刊预警名单-中国科学院文献情报中心 期刊分区表团队 |url=https://ewl.fenqubiao.com/#/zh-cn/early-warning-journal-list-2025 |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=ewl.fenqubiao.com}}</ref> In 2024, Finland's [[JUFO|Publication Forum]], which classifies publication channels for academic research, downgraded 193 MDPI journals to its lowest, level 0 rating.<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |last=Kincaid |first=Ellie |date=2024-12-24 |title=Finland Publication Forum will downgrade hundreds of Frontiers and MDPI journals |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2024/12/24/finland-publication-forum-will-downgrade-hundreds-of-frontiers-and-mdpi-journals/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=Retraction Watch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web |title=Grey area journals to level 0 |url=https://julkaisufoorumi.fi/en/news/grey-area-journals-level-0 |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=Publication Forum |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
MDPI traces its roots to '''Molecular Diversity Preservation International''', also abbreviated MDPI, which was founded by Shu-Kun Lin in 1996 as a chemical sample archive, with some scholarly publishing and conference activities.<ref name=":14" /> The second organisation, Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute, was founded in 2010, primarily as a publisher. All of MDPI's journals have been [[open access]] and since 2008 published under a [[Creative Commons Attribution License]] ([[CC BY]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mdpi.com/openaccess/|title= MDPI Open Access Information and Policy |year=2019|access-date=1 September 2019}}</ref>

=== Molecular Diversity Preservation International ===

Molecular Diversity Preservation International was founded and registered as a [[non-profit association]] ({{lang|de|[[Swiss Verein|Verein]]}}) by Shu-Kun Lin and Benoit R. Turin in Basel in 1996 to enable the deposit and exchange of rare molecular and biomolecular research samples.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=history>{{cite web |url=http://www.mdpi.com/about/history |title=History of MDPI |access-date=17 March 2014}}</ref>

The journal [[Molecules (journal)|''Molecules'']] was established in 1996 in collaboration with Springer-Verlag (now [[Springer Science+Business Media]]) in order to document the chemical samples of the MDPI collection. Several other journals were established by the MDPI Verein, including [[Entropy (journal)|''Entropy'']] (1999), the ''[[International Journal of Molecular Sciences]]'' (2000), [[Sensors (journal)|''Sensors'']] (2001), ''[[Marine Drugs]]'' (2003), and the ''[[International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health]]'' (2004). The publisher '''MDPI AG''' was spun off from MDPI Verein in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mdpi AG - Company Profile |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/1440515D:SW |access-date=June 28, 2025 |website=Bloomberg}}</ref>

MDPI Verein co-organized several [[academic conferences]], including the ''International Symposium on Frontiers in Molecular Science''. It also runs [[virtual conference]]s, such as the Electronic Conference on Synthetic Organic Chemistry, which was started in 1997. In 2010 MDPI launched the platform Sciforum.net to host virtual conferences. In 2014, various virtual conferences were hosted in the areas of synthetic organic chemistry, material sciences, sensors, and sustainability. In 2015, MDPI co-organized two physical conferences with and at the [[University of Basel]], the 4th Internationational Symposium on Sensor Science and the 5th World Sustainability Forum. Since 2015, scholars can organize their own conference for free on the Sciforum platform.{{Citation needed|date=September 2021}}

=== MDPI (Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute) ===
MDPI as a publisher of [[open-access]] [[scientific journal]]s was spun off from the Molecular Diversity Preservation International organization. It was formally registered by Shu-Kun Lin and Dietrich Rordorf in May 2010 with its official headquarters in Basel, Switzerland. Including Switzerland, MDPI has editorial offices in 11 countries, with five offices in China, two offices in both Romania and Serbia, and offices in the United Kingdom, Canada, Spain, Poland, Japan, Thailand, and Singapore.<ref name="UA" /><ref name=history /><ref>{{Cite web |title=MDPI {{!}} About |url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/contact |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=www.mdpi.com}}</ref>

The number of published papers has been growing significantly in the last decade with year over year growth of over 50% in 2017, 2018 and 2019, with 110,000 papers published in 2019.<ref name=":0" /> MDPI reported publishing 235,638 papers in 2021 alone.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MDPI {{!}} History |url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/history |access-date=2022-03-09 |website=www.mdpi.com}}</ref> In 2020, MDPI was the largest publisher of open access papers in the world and the 5th largest publisher overall in terms of journal paper output.<ref name=":0"/>

MDPI was an early pioneer of the special issue model for academic publishing. The special issues are collections of papers on a specific topic, handled by guest editors (as opposed to members of the journal's editorial board). Many special issue papers are invited, either by the journal staff or by the guest editors. Roughly 88% of MDPI papers are published in special issues.<ref name="Strain">{{cite journal|title=The strain on scientific publishing|author=Mark A. Hanson, Pablo Gómez Barreiro, Paolo Crosetto, Dan Brockington|journal=Quantitative Science Studies |date=2024|volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=823–843 |doi=10.1162/qss_a_00327  |doi-access=free|arxiv=2309.15884 }}</ref> The number of MDPI special issues has grown rapidly, alongside significant year-over-year growth in total papers published: in 2020, MDPI journals hosted a total of 6,756 special issues, compared to 39,587 special issues in 2021.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":10" /> However, only 10,504 of these 2021 special issues ultimately resulted in published papers. The number of special issues publishing papers rose to 17,777 in 2022.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":10" />

MDPI operates Scilit, a free multidisciplinary scholarly literature aggregator. A 2026 review in ''[[Katina Magazine]]'', published by [[Annual Reviews (publisher)|Annual Reviews]], reported that Scilit indexed approximately 190 million publications from nearly 30,000 publishers and described it as a useful supplementary discovery resource, while noting limitations compared with commercial bibliographic databases such as Web of Science and Scopus.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anwar |first=Ch Mahmood |date=2026-08-13 |title=Can This Massive, Free Aggregator Platform Compete with Commercial Giants? |url=https://katinamagazine.org/content/article/resource-reviews/2026/massive-multidisciplinary-free-aggregator-scilit |journal=Katina Magazine |language=en |doi=10.1146/katina-081326-1|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Controversies ==
MDPI has had a number of controversies from the scientific community relating to its paper selection and review processes and the quality of its publications.

=== "Who's Afraid of Peer Review?" sting ===
{{anchor|Sting}}In 2013, the MDPI journal ''Cancers'' rejected a fake paper submitted to it in the "[[Who's Afraid of Peer Review?]]" [[sting operation]].<ref>See the [https://www.science.org/doi/suppl/10.1126/science.2013.342.6154.342_60 Data and Documents] of {{cite journal<!-- -->|last1=Bohannon|first1=John|year=2013|title=Who's Afraid of Peer Review?|journal=Science|volume=342|issue=6154|pages=60–65|doi=10.1126/science.342.6154.60|pmid=24092725|doi-access=free|bibcode=2013Sci...342...60B}}</ref>

=== Inclusion in Beall's list ===
MDPI was included on [[Jeffrey Beall]]'s list of [[predatory open access publishing]] companies in February 2014.<ref name=Beall2014>{{cite web |last=Beall |first=Jeffrey |author-link=Jeffrey Beall |date=18 February 2014 |url=http://scholarlyoa.com/2014/02/18/chinese-publishner-mdpi-added-to-list-of-questionable-publishers/ |title=Chinese Publisher MDPI Added to List of Questionable Publishers |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306052944/http://scholarlyoa.com/2014/02/18/chinese-publishner-mdpi-added-to-list-of-questionable-publishers/ |archive-date=6 March 2014 |website=Scholarly Open Access }}</ref> Beall's concern was that "MDPI's warehouse journals contain hundreds of lightly-reviewed articles that are mainly written and published for promotion and tenure purposes rather than to communicate science."<ref name=Beall2014/> Beall also claimed that MDPI used [[email spam]] to solicit manuscripts<ref>{{cite web |last=Beall |first=Jeffery |author-link=Jeffrey Beall |date=11 June 2015 |url=http://scholarlyoa.com/2015/06/11/guest-editing-a-special-issue-with-mdpi-evidences-of-questionable-actions-by-the-publisher/ |title=Guest Editing a Special Issue with MDPI: Evidences of Questionable Actions by the Publisher |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150616230128/http://scholarlyoa.com/2015/06/11/guest-editing-a-special-issue-with-mdpi-evidences-of-questionable-actions-by-the-publisher/ |archive-date=16 June 2015 |website=Scholarly Open Access }}</ref> and that the company listed [[Nobel Prize|Nobel laureates]] on its journals' editorial boards without their knowledge.<ref name=Beall2014/> MDPI responded to Beall's claims, seeking to debunk them.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Update: Response to Mr. Jeffrey Beall's Repeated Attacks on MDPI |url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/534 |access-date=2023-03-16 |website=www.mdpi.com |language=en}}</ref> Chemist [[Peter Murray-Rust]] criticized the inclusion of MDPI in Beall's list, writing in a blog post that Beall's criticism of the publisher "lacks evidence" and was "irresponsible". Commenters on the blog post (including Beall himself) noted that, despite Murray-Rust claiming to have "no personal involvement with MDPI", he was listed on their website as a member of their editorial board.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Beall's criticism of MDPI lacks evidence and is irresponsible {{!}} petermr's blog |url=https://blogs.ch.cam.ac.uk/pmr/2014/02/18/bealls-criticism-of-mdpi-lacks-evidence-and-is-irresponsible/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>

MDPI made a successful appeal to the Beall's list appeals board in October 2015, and was removed from the list.<ref name="ASH2017" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Update: Response to Mr. Jeffrey Beall's Repeated Attacks on MDPI|url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/534|access-date=2022-02-19|website=www.mdpi.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Xia|first=Jingfeng|title=Predatory Publishing|date=2021|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-0-367-46532-2}}</ref> Even after its removal, Beall remained critical of MDPI; in December 2015 he wrote: "it is clear that MDPI sees peer review as merely a perfunctory step that publishers have to endure before publishing papers and accepting money from the authors," and "it's clear that MDPI's peer review is managed by clueless clerical staff in China."<ref>{{cite web |last=Beall |first=Jeffrey |author-link=Jeffrey Beall |date=17 December 2015 |url=https://scholarlyoa.com/2015/12/17/instead-of-a-peer-review-reviewer-sends-warning-to-authors/ |title=Instead of a Peer Review, Reviewer Sends Warning to Authors |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313073101/https://scholarlyoa.com/2015/12/17/instead-of-a-peer-review-reviewer-sends-warning-to-authors/ |archive-date=13 March 2016 |website=Scholarly Open Access }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=29 March 2021|title=Beall Twitter statement calling MDPI predatory in 2021|url=https://twitter.com/Jeffrey_Beall/status/1376534050656018435|access-date=18 February 2021|website=@jeffrey_beall}}</ref>

Beall's list was shut down in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web| last1=Brown | first1=Michael | editor-first1=Tim | editor-last1=Dean |url=https://theconversation.com/who-will-keep-predatory-science-journals-at-bay-now-that-jeffrey-bealls-blog-is-gone-71613|title = Who will keep predatory science journals at bay now that Jeffrey Beall's blog is gone?| date=20 January 2017 | doi=10.64628/AA.fa3gd5ery }}</ref> Beall later wrote that he had been pressured to shut down the list by both his employer, [[University of Colorado Denver]], and various publishers, specifically mentioning MDPI as a publisher that had "tried to be as annoying as possible to the university so that the officials would get so tired of the emails that they would silence me just to make them stop."<ref name="biochemia">{{cite journal|last=Beall|first=Jeffrey|year=2017|title=What I learned from predatory publishers|journal=Biochemia Medica|volume=27|issue=2|pages=273–279|doi=10.11613/BM.2017.029|pmc=5493177|pmid=28694718|quote=Still others tried different strategies. Some tried annoying university officials with numerous emails and letters, often sent as PDF attachments, with fancy letterhead, informing the university how I was hurting its reputation. They kept sending the emails to the university chancellor and others, hoping to implement the heckler's veto. They tried to be as annoying as possible to the university so that the officials would get so tired of the emails that they would silence me just to make them stop. The publisher MDPI used this strategy.|doi-access=free}}</ref> Although his supervisor insisted that the university had supported Beall,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Swauger |first=Shea |date=2017-12-04 |title=Open access, power, and privilege: A response to "What I learned from predatory publishing" |url=https://crln.acrl.org/index.php/crlnews/article/view/16837 |journal=College & Research Libraries News |language=en |volume=78 |issue=11 |page=603 |doi=10.5860/crln.78.11.603 |issn=2150-6698 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616230236/https://crln.acrl.org/index.php/crlnews/article/view/16837 |archive-date=16 June 2025 |access-date=28 June 2025 |url-status=live |doi-access=free }}</ref> the university did open a research misconduct review of Beall's listing of another open access publisher, [[Frontiers Media]]. The investigation closed without findings.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-09-13 |title=Why Beall's List Died — and What It Left Unresolved About Open Access |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/why-bealls-list-died-and-what-it-left-unresolved-about-open-access/ |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2014 OASPA evaluation ===
Following Beall's criticism of MDPI, the [[Open Access Scholarly Publishers Association]] (OASPA) conducted an investigation in April 2014. This investigation was based on the controversy surrounding two papers, one in ''[[Life (journal)|Life]]'',<ref name=andrulis/> the other in ''[[Nutrients (journal)|Nutrients]]'';<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.3390/nu3040491|pmid = 22254107|pmc = 3257688|title = The Australian Paradox: A Substantial Decline in Sugars Intake over the Same Timeframe that Overweight and Obesity Have Increased|journal = Nutrients|volume = 3|issue = 4|pages = 491–504|year = 2011|last1 = Barclay|first1 = Alan W.|last2 = Brand-Miller|first2 = Jennie|doi-access = free}}</ref> the listing of Nobel Prize winners on the website; the roles of editorial board members and of Shu-Kun Lin within the company; and the functions of the different office locations. OASPA concluded that MDPI satisfactorily meets the OASPA Membership Criteria.<ref name=OASPA-Conclusions>{{cite web |last=Redhead |first=Claire |title=Conclusions from OASPA Membership Committee Investigation into MDPI |work=OASPA |url=https://oaspa.org/conclusions-from-oaspa-membership-committee-investigation-into-mdpi/ |date=11 April 2014 |access-date=5 January 2019 |archive-date=5 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305033831/https://www.oaspa.org/conclusions-from-oaspa-membership-committee-investigation-into-mdpi/ }}</ref>

===2016 data breach===
In August 2016, MDPI was [[security breach|breached]], leaving exposed 17.5 GB of data, including 845,000 e-mail addresses and e-mail exchanges between authors, editors and reviewers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.itsecuritynews.info/mdpi-845012-breached-accounts/|title=MDPI – 845,012 breached accounts|last=www.ITSecurityNews.info|date=26 March 2018|work=IT Security News - cybersecurity, infosecurity news|access-date=12 August 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=12 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812151209/https://www.itsecuritynews.info/mdpi-845012-breached-accounts/}}</ref> According to MDPI, the unprotected instance at which the data was breached has since been protected.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Have I Been Pwned: Pwned websites |url=https://haveibeenpwned.com/PwnedWebsites |publisher=haveibeenpwned.com}}</ref>

=== Resignations of editors ===

In August 2018, 10 senior editors (including the editor-in-chief) of the journal ''[[Nutrients (journal)|Nutrients]]'' resigned, alleging that MDPI forced the replacement of the editor-in-chief because of his high editorial standards and for resisting pressure to "accept manuscripts of mediocre quality and importance."<ref name=Vrieze>{{cite journal |doi=10.1126/science.aav3129|title=Open-access journal editors resign after alleged pressure to publish mediocre papers|journal=Science|year=2018|last1=de Vrieze|first1=Jop|s2cid=158215919|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/open-access-editors-resign-after-alleged-pressure-publish-mediocre-papers |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224022058/http://www.sciencemag.org/news/2018/09/open-access-editors-resign-after-alleged-pressure-publish-mediocre-papers|archive-date=24 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2020, the would-be guest editors of a special issue in the ''International Journal of Environmental Research and Health'' resigned after being informed by an MDPI representative that a quota of publication-fee exemptions allocated to the special issue could only be given to scholars from developed countries.<ref>{{Cite web|title="What the F?": How we failed to publish a journal special issue on failures: Water, Sanitation and Health (WASH) Blog|url=https://wash.leeds.ac.uk/what-the-f-how-we-failed-to-publish-a-journal-special-issue-on-failures/|access-date=17 June 2020|website=wash.leeds.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Marcus|first=Adam|date=16 June 2020|title=Failure fails as publisher privileges the privileged|url=https://retractionwatch.com/2020/06/16/failure-fails-as-publisher-privileges-the-privileged/|access-date=17 June 2020|website=Retraction Watch|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2021, five members of the editorial board of the journal ''[[Vaccines (journal)|Vaccines]]'' resigned after ''Vaccines'' published a controversial article that misused data to reach the incorrect conclusion that vaccines against COVID-19 had no clear benefit.<ref name=":2" /><ref name="sciencemag" />

===Withdrawals of support by faculties and universities ===
In December 2021, the Faculty of Science of the [[University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice]] announced that it will stop financial support for publishing in MDPI journals, officially recommended against publishing in or reviewing for MDPI, and warned that publications in MDPI journals might not be taken into account for evaluations of employees and departments.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prf.jcu.cz/data/files/498/530/6405mdpi.pdf|title=Regulation of the management of FSc USB concerning publishing in journals published by MDPI|date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209092716/https://www.prf.jcu.cz/data/files/498/530/6405mdpi.pdf|archive-date=9 December 2021}}</ref> In January 2023, [[Zhejiang Gongshang University]] ({{Lang|zh|浙江工商大学}}) in Hangzhou, China, announced it would no longer include articles published in [[Hindawi (publisher)|Hindawi]], MDPI, and [[Frontiers Media|Frontiers]] journals when evaluating researcher performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ForeignFriends |title=MDPI, Frontiers & Hindawi are blacklisted by a university |url=http://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MjM5OTY5OTU0Nw==&mid=2454145404&idx=1&sn=e4c8a9cb19c88c120946a4d65403cb0e&chksm=b0849c4887f3155e23aad0563c372f92a6cfdbc8e7fa828ccfc54ec6ccde229cee15e6a49247#rd |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=Weixin Official Accounts Platform}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=弗雷赛斯-freescience |date=2023-01-08 |title=霸气！这所高校直接将Frontiers、MDPI、Hindawi三个出版社的所有期刊都纳入黑名单！ |url=https://t.cj.sina.cn/articles/view/6468995530/1819509ca019011lpg?from=tech |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=t.cj.sina.cn}}</ref>

=== Inclusion in Early Warning List of the Chinese Academy of Sciences ===
In December 2020, the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] published a list of journals that may suffer from issues of scientific quality and other risk characteristics.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=CoS partition table team|first=Chinese Academy of Sciences|date=31 December 2020|title=《国际期刊预警名单（试行）》正式发布 - "International Journal Early Warning List officially released (Trial)"|url=https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MzI1MzA2MzM1NA==&mid=2659567089&idx=1&sn=f4cad93ba3a425524eb19d25ffb25960&chksm=f2ab5c24c5dcd53275aa36b9167d9788577a6a919e2bc80b1144088ea78b32bae8350535b344&scene=0&xtrack=1|access-date=1 January 2022|website=mp.weixin.qq}}</ref> There were 22 MDPI group journals in the 65 journals given in its initial list. MDPI responded to the list promising to communicate with the academy and improve its journals' parameters to remove the affected journals from the list as soon as possible.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MDPI|first=China Marketing Department|date=7 January 2021|title=关于中科院发布《国际期刊预警名单（试行）》的声明 Announcement on the Chinese Academy of Sciences' release of the "Warning List of International Journals (Trial)"|url=https://mdpi.cn/announcements/284|access-date=1 January 2022|website=MDPI}}</ref> The list was updated in December 2021 and reduced to only 41 journals, of which seven MDPI journals were included.<ref>{{Cite web|last=CoS partition table team|first=Chinese Academy of Sciences|date=31 December 2021|title=《国际期刊预警名单（试行）》正式发布 - "International Journal Early Warning List officially released (Trial)"|url=https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MzI1MzA2MzM1NA==&mid=2659568109&idx=1&sn=576f0a8198b7f58fb4e4c9d410ebf5e8&chksm=f2ab5038c5dcd92e4b91149cb2348a9c6ea163fd61f6391efc8cdd80f0d7f3b7bdbbaab89db9&scene=178&cur_album_id=1634277489231314948#rd|access-date=1 January 2022|website=mp.weixin.qq}}</ref> In the 2025 revision of the list, all MDPI journals were removed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Early Warning Journal List 2025 Released by the Chinese Academy of Sciences |url=https://libguides.library.cityu.edu.hk/rssc_blog/home/Early-Warning-Journal-List-2025-Released-by-the-Chinese-Academy-of-Sciences |website=Research Support and Scholarly Communications Blog |publisher=City University of Hong Kong Library |access-date=2025-07-16}}</ref>{{fv|date=February 2026}}

=== Perception among Hungarian researchers ===
A survey published in 2022 asked Hungarian researchers for their perception of MDPI journals. Those Hungarian researchers generally felt MDPI journals were sufficiently prestigious to be worth publishing in, being indexed in major databases and having reasonable [[journal impact factor]]. However, most researchers felt the primary driving force to publish with MDPI journals was their fast article turnaround time.<ref name="Csomos" /> In 2019–2020, MDPI articles took 35–37 days on average for acceptance (including revisions),<ref name=":5"/><ref name=":4" /> and 41 days to publish the final article online after its initial submission, as compared to an industry average of 163 days.<ref name=":4" />

=== Assessments in the Nordic countries ===
MDPI has been criticized by scientific bodies in Norway, Finland, and Denmark that rank academic journals for their quality and relevance. In the Finnish and Danish lists, the majority of MDPI journals do not meet the criteria of the body to be ranked in the list.<ref name="UA" /><ref>{{cite web |title=The BFI lists |url=https://ufm.dk/en/research-and-innovation/statistics-and-analyses/bibliometric-research-indicator/bfi-lists |access-date=2 May 2020 |publisher=[[Ministry of Higher Education and Science (Denmark)|Ministry of Higher Education and Science]]}}</ref> The [[Norwegian Scientific Index]] has been less critical, giving the vast majority of individual MDPI journals designations as "level 1", their "standard" rating denoting a publisher as academic; although some journals are ranked "level 0" denoting non-academic status, including one of MDPI's flagship journals, [[Sustainability (journal)|''Sustainability'']].<ref name="NorwegianScientificIndex">{{cite web|author=<!--Not stated-->|title=MDPI|url=https://kanalregister.hkdir.no/publiseringskanaler/KanalForlagInfo.action?id=26778&bibsys=false|url-status=live|archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20191127194701/http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=https://dbh.nsd.uib.no/publiseringskanaler/KanalForlagInfo.action?id=26778&bibsys=false|archive-date=27 November 2019|access-date=21 July 2019|website=[[Norwegian Scientific Index]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Forlag info {{!}} Kanalregisteret |url=https://kanalregister.hkdir.no/publiseringskanaler/KanalForlagInfo.action?id=26778 |access-date=2022-06-01 |website=kanalregister.hkdir.no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Stryker et av verdens største fra listen over godkjente tidsskrifter |work=Khrono |url=https://khrono.no/stryker-et-av-verdens-storste-fra-listen-over-godkjente-tidsskrifter/689264 |access-date=22 May 2022}}</ref> In 2021, following a survey sent to Norwegian scientists,<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Børresen |first1=Anne Kristine |last2=Røeggen |first2=Vidar |last3=Sivertsen |first3=Gunnar |date=16 January 2020 |title=Innlegg: Forlag sluker forfatterbetaling |url=https://www.dn.no/innlegg/forskning/forlag/vitenskap/innlegg-forlag-sluker-forfatterbetaling/2-1-736132 |access-date=2 March 2021 |website=www.dn.no}}</ref> the Norwegian Scientific Index also created a special rank called "level X", which was used to denote journals undergoing evaluation as possible predatory journals, specifically citing concerns over MDPI journals for the new rank's creation.<ref name="khrono2021" />

The head of the National Publication Committee of Norway and a number of Norwegian scholars have been highly critical of MDPI, with some lobbying to remove MDPI from the Norwegian Scientific Index entirely.<ref name="UA" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Børresen |first1=Anne Kristine |last2=Røeggen |first2=Vidar |last3=Sivertsen |first3=Gunnar |date=16 January 2020 |title=Forlag sluker forfatterbetaling |url=https://www.dn.no/innlegg/forskning/forlag/vitenskap/innlegg-forlag-sluker-forfatterbetaling/2-1-736132 |journal=[[Dagens Næringsliv]]}}</ref> They cite the poor reputation of MDPI among Nordic scientific bodies,<ref name="UA" /> how there are many academics that boycott MDPI journals outright,<ref name="UA" /> or accuse MDPI journals of having a peer review process that is not up to academic standards.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ellingsen |first=Simen Andreas Ådnøy |author-link=Simen Andreas Ådnøy Ellingsen |date=21 October 2019 |title=Faren med kommersiell Open Access |trans-title=The danger of commercial open access |work=Universitetsavisa |url=https://www.universitetsavisa.no/ytring/2019/10/21/Faren-med-kommersiell-Open-Access-20215796.ece}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{cite web |last1=Nøland |first1=Jonas Kristiansen |last2=Fosso |first2=Olav Bjarte |author-link2=Olav Bjarte Fosso |date=25 May 2021 |title=Profittjegere vanner ut norsk forskning |trans-title=Profit hunters dilute Norwegian research |url=https://khrono.no/profittjegere-vanner-ut-norsk-forskning/581783 |access-date=25 May 2021 |website=Khrono}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{cite news |title=Dårlig og farlig forskning |trans-title=Bad and dangerous research |work=VG |url=https://www.vg.no/nyheter/meninger/i/LnvX0x/daarlig-og-farlig-forskning |access-date=9 July 2021}}</ref> Among their descriptions, they call MDPI a Chinese organization with a "small artificial office in Switzerland",<ref name="UA" /> and "a money-making machine" that plays on the desire of academics to embellish their CV.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" />

=== Allegation of anomalous citation patterns===
In July 2021, Maria Ángeles Oviedo-García published a paper in [[Oxford University Press|OUP]] journal ''[[Research Evaluation]]'' claiming that MDPI journals had anomalously high self-citation rates compared to leading journals in the same fields. The alleged high self-citation rate is not to other articles in the same journal, but rather to other MDPI journals.<ref name=Oviedo-García>{{cite journal|last=Ángeles Oviedo-García|first=Maria|date=11 August 2021|title=Journal citation reports and the definition of a predatory journal: The case of the Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute (MDPI)|url=https://academic.oup.com/rev/article/30/3/405/6348133|journal=Research Evaluation|volume=30 |issue=3 |pages=405–419a|doi=10.1093/reseval/rvab030 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Oviedo-García argued that this is indicative of predatory journals. MDPI released a response to Oviedo-García's paper on their website eight days later. MDPI highlighted a number of issues with the article and its framing, arguing in particular that leading journals should not be directly compared to non-leading journals; MDPI also argued that, when compared to other publishers, MDPI does not have anomalously high self-citations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/2979|title=Comment on: 'Journal citation reports and the definition of a predatory journal: The case of the Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute (MDPI)' from Oviedo-García|date=19 August 2021|author=Giulia Stefenelli}}</ref> ''Research Evaluation'' published an expression of concern for Oviedo-García's paper in September 2021,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://academic.oup.com/rev/article/30/3/420/6360986|title=Expression of concern: Journal citation reports and the definition of a predatory journal: The case of the Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute (MDPI)|date=1 September 2021|journal=Research Evaluation|doi=10.1093/reseval/rvab030 |last1=Ángeles Oviedo-García |first1=M. |volume=30 |issue=3 |page=420 }}</ref> which eventually led to a correction published in April 2023. Changes made to the article added caveats and toned down inflammatory language, however the core conclusions remained the same.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://retractionwatch.com/2023/05/08/article-that-assessed-mdpi-journals-as-predatory-retracted-and-replaced/|title=Article that assessed MDPI journals as "predatory" retracted and replaced|publisher=Retraction Watch|date=8 May 2023}}</ref>

A 2023 study utilizing a different method reached a broadly similar conclusion that MDPI journals had more self-citations than journals by other publishers. The study also found that MDPI journals received more citations from a smaller network of journals, relative to journals by other publishers.<ref name="Strain" />

=== Concerns over papers connected to a research paper mill ===

In December 2021, it was reported how the [[research paper mill]] [[International Publisher Ltd.]] had sold authorships to hundreds of publications published across most major publishers;<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-02 |title=Economist Investigates Hijacked Journals in Scholarship |url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/en/featured-stories/research/2022/hijacked-journals/index.html |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=Freie Universität Berlin campus.leben |language=en}}</ref> a controversy attracting international attention that affected many major publishing groups.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russian site peddles paper authorship in reputable journals for up to $5000 a pop |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/russian-website-peddles-authorships-linked-reputable-journals |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Publication and Collaboration Anomalies in Academic Papers Originating From a Russian-Based Paper Mill |url=https://peerreviewcongress.org/abstract/publication-and-collaboration-anomalies-in-academic-papers-originating-from-a-russian-based-paper-mill/ |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=Peer Review Congress |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=2022-01-19 |title=Academic fraud factories are booming, warns plagiarism sleuth |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/academic-fraud-factories-are-booming-warns-plagiarism-sleuth |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=Times Higher Education |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Else |first=Holly |date=2023-01-18 |title=Multimillion-dollar trade in paper authorships alarms publishers |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-023-00062-9 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=613 |issue=7945 |pages=617–618 |doi=10.1038/d41586-023-00062-9|pmid=36653614 |bibcode=2023Natur.613..617E |s2cid=255970642 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> The report highlighted a ring of MDPI guest editors that provided a network for the sale of authorship for articles published across multiple MDPI journals ([[Sustainability (journal)|''Sustainability'']], ''Mathematics, Energies'', and the ''Journal of Theoretical and Applied Commerce Research'').<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Abalkina |first=Anna |author-link=Anna Abalkina |date=2023 |title=Publication and collaboration anomalies in academic papers originating from a paper mill: Evidence from a Russia-based paper mill |journal=Learned Publishing |volume=36 |issue=4 |pages=689–702 |arxiv=2112.13322 |doi=10.1002/leap.1574 |doi-access=free |s2cid=247595393}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Abalkina, Anna |first=ENAI Monthly Webinars |date=2023-02-10 |title=The rising threat of Paper Mills |url=https://www.academicintegrity.eu/wp/enai-monthly-webinars/ |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=European Network for Academic Integrity |language=en-GB}}</ref> Also in December 2021, Dr. Brian Perron highlighted how International Publisher Ltd. had published articles in the ''International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJet)'', and MDPI including articles from ''Energies''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-21 |title=Ghostwriting and Academic Fraud |url=https://www.caperay.com/blog/ghostwriting-and-academic-fraud/ |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=CapeRay |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last1=Perron |first1=Brian E. |last2=Hiltz-Perron |first2=Oliver T. |last3=Victor |first3=Bryan G. |date=20 December 2021 |title=Revealed: The inner workings of a paper mill |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2021/12/20/revealed-the-inner-workings-of-a-paper-mill/ |access-date=15 March 2023 |website=Retraction Watch}}</ref> In response, ''iJet'' retracted thirty articles, and thanked Perron and his team for their concerning findings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Recently Retracted Articles |url=https://online-journals.org/index.php/i-jet/announcement/view/17 |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning}}</ref> In response, Damaris Critchlow from MDPI stated that MDPI was investigating the papers in question and developing strategies to combat paper mills.<ref name=":13" /> Perron later expressed appreciation with how ''iJet'' had handled its response, but frustration with MDPI for not taking his allegations of fraud seriously, citing how one ''Energies'' article still did not even have an [[expression of concern]] added six months later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Perron |first=Brian E. |title='Our deepest apology': Journal retracts 30 likely paper mill articles after investigation published by Retraction Watch |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2022/07/05/our-deepest-apology-journal-retracts-30-likely-paper-mill-articles-after-investigation-published-by-retraction-watch/ |access-date=15 March 2021 |website=Retraction Watch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Milojević |first1=Marko |last2=Urbański |first2=Mariusz |last3=Terzić |first3=Ivica |last4=Prasolov |first4=Valeriy |date=2020 |title=Impact of Non-Financial Factors on the Effectiveness of Audits in Energy Companies |journal=Energies |language=en |volume=13 |issue=23 |page=6212 |doi=10.3390/en13236212 |issn=1996-1073|doi-access=free }}</ref>

===2023 Clarivate delistings===
In February 2023, [[Clarivate]] discontinued coverage of two MDPI journals, the ''[[International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health]]'' and the ''[[Journal of Risk and Financial Management]]'' in the [[Web of Science]], for publishing content not related to their scope.<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |title=Clarivate Discontinues IJERPH and JRFM Coverage in Web of Science |url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/5536 |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=MDPI}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Fast-growing open-access journals stripped of coveted impact factors |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/fast-growing-open-access-journals-stripped-coveted-impact-factors |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref> As a result, both were removed from the Clarivate Web of Science database, losing their [[impact factor]]s. Also, citations from these journals no longer affect the impact factors of other journals.<ref name=":11" /><ref name=":12" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Petrou |first=Christos |date=2023-03-30 |title=Guest Post – Of Special Issues and Journal Purges |url=https://scholarlykitchen.sspnet.org/2023/03/30/guest-post-of-special-issues-and-journal-purges/ |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=The Scholarly Kitchen |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2024 Finnish downgrading ===
In December 2024, Finland's [[JUFO|Publication Forum]] (JUFO), which classifies publication channels for academic research, downgraded 193 MDPI journals to its lowest, level 0 rating. These are outside the organization's 3 level scale and receive the same points in funding applications as popular articles or publications without peer-review. JUFO referred to these publications as "grey area journals", including journals from [[Frontiers Media|Frontiers]] along those of MDPI's. The organization decided to retain the previous, level 1 rating for 16 MDPI journals.<ref name=":15" /><ref name=":16" />

=== Controversial articles ===
In December 2011, the MDPI journal ''[[Life (journal)|Life]]'' published Erik D. Andrulis' theoretical paper, "Theory of the Origin, Evolution, and Nature of Life", which claimed to present a unified [[theory of everything]], asserting that the basis of all matter and energy in the universe, including [[Subatomic particle|subatomic particles]], is something which the author refers to as "gyres".<ref name=andrulis>{{cite journal |last=Andrulis |first=Erik D. |title=Theory of the Origin, Evolution, and Nature of Life |journal=Life |date=2011 |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=1–105 |doi=10.3390/life2010001 |pmid=25382118 |pmc=4187144 |bibcode=2011Life....2....1A |doi-access=free}}</ref> It attracted coverage by the [[popular science]] and technology magazines ''[[Ars Technica]]'' and ''[[Popular Science]]'', which described it as "crazy"<ref>{{cite news |last=Timmer |first=John |title=How the craziest f#@!ing "theory of everything" got published and promoted |url=https://arstechnica.com/science/2012/01/how-the-craziest-fing-theory-of-everything-got-published-and-promoted/ |access-date=17 January 2014 |newspaper=Ars Technica}}</ref> and "hilarious".<ref name="popscilifepaper">{{cite news |last=Nosowitz |first=Dan |title=Hilarious "Theory of Everything" Paper Provokes Kerfuffle |url=http://www.popsci.com/science/article/2012-02/hilarious-theory-everything-paper-provokes-kerfuffle-hullabaloo-foofaraw |access-date=17 January 2014 |newspaper=Popular Science}}</ref> A member of ''Life''<nowiki/>'s [[editorial board]] resigned in response.<ref name="popscilifepaper"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Zimmer |first=Carl |title=Life turned upside down |url=http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/loom/2012/01/31/life-turned-upside-down/#.Utj4jvS1zFV |access-date=17 January 2014 |newspaper=Discover Magazine}}</ref>

In 2013, another MDPI journal, ''[[Entropy (journal)|Entropy]]'', published a [[Review article|review paper]] claiming that [[glyphosate]] may be the most consequential factor in the development of [[obesity]], [[Depression (mood)|depression]], [[attention deficit hyperactivity disorder]], [[autism]], [[Alzheimer's disease]], [[Parkinson's disease]], [[multiple sclerosis]], [[cancer]], and [[infertility]].<ref name="samsel">{{cite journal |last=Samsel |first=Anthony |author2=Seneff |title=Glyphosate's Suppression of Cytochrome P450 Enzymes and Amino Acid Biosynthesis by the Gut Microbiome: Pathways to Modern Diseases |journal=Entropy |volume=15 |issue=4 |page=1416 |doi=10.3390/e15041416 |doi-access=free  |bibcode=2013Entrp..15.1416S |year=2013 |hdl=1721.1/79612 |hdl-access=free |first2=Stephanie|author-link2=Stephanie Seneff}}</ref> The paper itself does not contain any primary research results.<ref name=samsel /> It was criticized as [[pseudo-science]] by popular science magazine [[Discover (magazine)|''Discover'']].<ref>{{cite news |last=Kloor |first=Keith |title=When Media Uncritically Cover Pseudoscience |url=http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/collideascape/2013/04/26/when-media-uncritically-cover-pseudoscience/#.UtkD__S1zFU |access-date=17 January 2014 |newspaper=Discover Magazine |archive-date=29 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140129002742/http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/collideascape/2013/04/26/when-media-uncritically-cover-pseudoscience/#.UtkD__S1zFU }}</ref> [[Jeffrey Beall]] noted that both of the paper's authors, Anthony Samsel and [[Stephanie Seneff]], had backgrounds in computer science rather than biochemistry or human disease, and wrote, "When publishers like MDPI disseminate research by science activists like Stephanie Seneff and her co-authors, I think it's fair to question the credibility of all the research that MDPI publishes. Will MDPI publish anything for money?".<ref name="Beall2015">{{cite web|title=Anti-Roundup (Glyphosate) Researchers Use Easy OA Journals to Spread their Views |url=http://scholarlyoa.com/2015/01/08/anti-roundup-glyphosate-researchers-use-easy-oa-journals-to-spread-their-views/ |website=Scholarly Open Access |access-date=8 January 2015 |last1=Beall |first1=Jeffrey |author-link=Jeffrey Beall |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150112022110/http://scholarlyoa.com/2015/01/08/anti-roundup-glyphosate-researchers-use-easy-oa-journals-to-spread-their-views/ |archive-date=12 January 2015 }}</ref>

A study published in the MDPI journal [[Nutrients (journal)|''Nutrients'']] in 2011 went through a series of corrections, first in August 2011, then in April 2012, and then again in February 2014.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Barclay|first1=Alan W.|last2=Brand-Miller|first2=Jennie|date=2011-04-20|title=The Australian Paradox: A Substantial Decline in Sugars Intake over the Same Timeframe that Overweight and Obesity Have Increased|journal=Nutrients|language=en|volume=3|issue=4|pages=491–504|doi=10.3390/nu3040491|issn=2072-6643|pmc=3257688|pmid=22254107|doi-access=free}}</ref> The article claimed that obesity rates in Australia had increased over the same period of time that sugary [[soft drink]] consumption declined by 10%. The article was used by soft drink industry lobbyists to argue that sugary drinks were not significantly contributing to obesity rates.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|last=Wendy|first=Carlisle|date=February 13, 2014|title=Sugar research paper contained 'inadvertent errors'; Professor Jennie Brand-Miller defends findings|work=ABC News|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-02-13/errors-force-nutritionists-to-correct-controversial-sugar-paper/5258024|access-date=November 25, 2021}}</ref> However the article itself debunked its own claim, with one figure showing that sugary soft drink consumption had increased by 30% during the time period where the authors claimed a 10% reduction in consumption. ''Nutrients'' issued a correction claiming that the previously described 10% drop in consumption referred to an increase in the use of [[Sugar substitute|artificial sweeteners]], and reflected overall sugar consumption rather than soft drink consumption. The correction said that "some words were missing." This correction has been derided by some as "nonsense" and untrue, suggesting that it does not address the core issue of whether sugary soft drink consumption increased in Australia over the time period investigated. The journal ''Nutrients'' and the senior author of the article maintain that the thrice-corrected article is now accurate, and that corrections that were made were immaterial to the conclusions of the study.<ref name=":1" />

In 2016, MDPI journal ''[[Behavioral Sciences (journal)|Behavioral Sciences]]'' published a review paper that claimed that watching pornography is a cause of [[erectile dysfunction]].<ref name = OrigEDpaper>{{cite journal|doi = 10.3390/bs6030017|pmc = 5039517|pmid = 27527226|title = Is Internet Pornography Causing Sexual Dysfunctions? A Review with Clinical Reports.|journal = [[Behavioral Sciences (journal)|Behavioral Sciences]]|volume = 6|issue = 3|page = 17|year = 2016|last1 = Park|first1 = Brian Y.|last2 = Wilson|first2 = Gary|last3 = Berger|first3 = Jonathan|last4 = Christman|first4 = Matthew|last5 = Reina|first5 = Bryn|last6 = Bishop|first6 = Frank|last7 = Klam|first7 = Warren|last8 = Doan|first8 = Andrew P.|doi-access = free}}{{Erratum|doi=10.3390/bs8060055|pmid=29857562|http://retractionwatch.com/2018/06/13/journal-corrects-but-will-not-retract-controversial-paper-on-internet-porn/ ''Retraction Watch''|checked=yes|doi-access=free}}</ref> After critics raised concerns, an independent review by the [[Committee on Publication Ethics]] (COPE) recommended that the article be retracted, based on issues including an unusual editorial process in which the listed journal editor declared that he "was not involved in the final decision regarding correction/retraction/authorship," an inaccurate and incomplete conflict of interest declaration that failed to disclose author connections with anti-pornography activist groups, failure to obtain informed consent from the study subjects, and failure to protect the identities of those subjects. Instead of retracting the paper, MDPI removed the editor's name from the paper and issued an amended conflict of interest statement which, according to [[Retraction Watch]], did not fully address the conflicts of interest identified by COPE, nor the other issues identified by them. When contacted by Retraction Watch, MDPI's response was "The argument is already done. Both sides got large audience. Time to stop and made peace."<ref name="retractionwatch.com">{{cite web |last=Marcus |first=Adam |title= Journal corrects, but will not retract, controversial paper on internet porn |url= https://retractionwatch.com/2018/06/13/journal-corrects-but-will-not-retract-controversial-paper-on-internet-porn/|access-date=13 June 2018|website=Retraction Watch |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180614175449/https://retractionwatch.com/2018/06/13/journal-corrects-but-will-not-retract-controversial-paper-on-internet-porn/|archive-date=14 June 2018|date=13 June 2018 }}</ref>

The journal ''Magnetochemistry'' accepted a paper in 2019 by controversial researcher [[Susan Pockett]] which stated that "scientists are suppressing evidence that [[Microwave|microwave radiation]] from smartphones and other devices cause harm to people". The paper was later that year retracted due to lack of a scientific contribution and being an opinion article. The journal initially invited Susan Pockett to submit a paper, according to the author's own account.<ref>{{cite web |title='No scientific contribution': Journal pulls paper alleging radiation coverup |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2019/09/09/no-scientific-contribution-journal-pulls-paper-alleging-radiation-coverup/ |website=Retraction Watch |date=9 September 2019 }}</ref>

In 2019, MDPI journal ''Psych'' published an editorial on [[race and intelligence]] by [[Richard Lynn]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lynn |first1=Richard |title=Reflections on Sixty-Eight Years of Research on Race and Intelligence |journal=Psych |date=24 April 2019 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=123–131 |doi=10.3390/psych1010009 |doi-access=free }}{{Expression of Concern|doi=10.3390/psych1010033|http://retractionwatch.com/2019/08/08/prof-who-lost-emeritus-status-for-views-on-race-and-intelligence-has-paper-flagged/ ''Retraction Watch''|intentional=yes|doi-access=free}}</ref> who had previously had his emeritus status revoked due to his promotion of discredited sexist and racist views, such as [[scientific racism]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Status withdrawn from controversial academic |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-43768132 |access-date=11 May 2020 |work=BBC News |date=14 April 2018}}</ref><ref name = "RW">{{cite web |last1=Oransky |first1=Ivan |title=Prof who lost emeritus status for views on race and intelligence has paper flagged |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2019/08/08/prof-who-lost-emeritus-status-for-views-on-race-and-intelligence-has-paper-flagged/ |website=Retraction Watch |access-date=10 January 2020|date=8 August 2019 }}</ref> MDPI later issued an expression of concern and changed the status of the article from editorial to opinion, three months after publication.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Standifer|first=Cid|title=Racial Pseudoscience on the Faculty: A professor's research flew under the radar for years. What finally got him fired?|journal=The Chronicle of Higher Education|date=13 October 2022|url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/racial-pseudoscience-on-the-faculty?cid=at&source=ams&sourceid=&cid2=gen_login_refresh}}</ref> According to science journalist [[Angela Saini]], ''Psych'' had also published other similar work defending scientific racism.<ref name = "EoC">{{cite journal |author=Psych Editorial Office |title=Expression of Concern: Lynn, R. Reflections on Sixty-Eight Years of Research on Race and Intelligence |journal=Psych |date=2019 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=429–430 |doi=10.3390/psych1010033 |language=en|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name = "RW" />

In 2021, the MDPI journal ''[[Vaccines (journal)|Vaccines]]'' published an article by pseudoscience advocate [[Harald Walach]] and colleagues claiming a "lack of clear benefit" for [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccines]].<ref name="ansede">{{cite news |last1=Ansede |first1=Manuel |last2=Urra |first2=Susana |title=Harald Walach, the researcher contributing misinformation about the Covid-19 pandemic |url=https://english.elpais.com/usa/2021-07-22/harald-walach-the-researcher-contributing-misinformation-about-the-covid-19-pandemic.html |work=EL PAÍS |date=22 July 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.3390/vaccines9070693 | doi-access = free | title = The Safety of COVID-19 Vaccinations—We Should Rethink the Policy | year = 2021 | last1 = Walach | first1 = Harald | author-link1 = Harald Walach | last2 = Klement | first2 = Rainer J. | last3 = Aukema | first3 = Wouter | journal = Vaccines | volume = 9 | issue = 7 | page = 693 | pmid = 34202529 | pmc = 8294615 }} {{Retracted|doi=10.3390/vaccines9070729|pmid=34232371|http://retractionwatch.com/2021/07/02/journal-retracts-paper-claiming-two-deaths-from-covid-19-vaccination-for-every-three-prevented-cases/ ''Retraction Watch''|http://retractionwatch.com/2021/06/29/paper-claiming-two-deaths-from-covid-19-vaccination-for-every-three-prevented-cases-earns-expression-of-concern/ ''Retraction Watch''|http://retractionwatch.com/2021/07/07/university-terminates-affiliation-with-researcher-who-had-paper-on-covid-19-vaccines-retracted-as-mask-study-comes-under-scrutiny/ ''Retraction Watch''|http://retractionwatch.com/retracted-coronavirus-covid-19-papers/ ''Retraction Watch''|intentional=yes|doi-access=free}}</ref>  The article was heavily criticized for misusing data and as a result reaching a false conclusion.<ref name=sciencemag>{{Cite journal| first = Meredith | last = Wadman | title = Scientists quit journal board, protesting 'grossly irresponsible' study claiming COVID-19 vaccines kill | url = https://www.science.org/content/article/scientists-quit-journal-board-protesting-grossly-irresponsible-study-claiming-covid-19 | journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]] | date = 1 July 2021 | access-date = 2 July 2021 |doi=10.1126/science.abk2629| s2cid = 243092907 }}</ref>  [[Katie Ewer]], one of the journal's editors, called the publication of the article "grossly irresponsible" and resigned from the editorial board as a protest against its publication.<ref name=sciencemag/>  Subsequently, four other members of the editorial board also resigned. Shortly afterwards, the journal published an "expression of concern" regarding the article and opened an investigation into the review process.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.3390/vaccines9070705 | doi-access = free | title = Expression of Concern: Walach et al. The Safety of COVID-19 Vaccinations—We Should Rethink the Policy. Vaccines 2021, 9, 693 | year = 2021 | last1 = Office | first1 = Vaccines Editorial | journal = Vaccines | volume = 9 | issue = 7 | page = 705 | pmid = 34203423 | pmc = 8294614 }}</ref><ref name=sciencemag /> The paper had received three reviewer reports (which the journal later made public)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mdpi.com/2076-393X/9/7/693/review_report|title=Vaccines review report|date=24 June 2021|access-date=22 December 2021}}</ref> which were, however, not very detailed and had apparently been written by reviewers who did not have topic expertise.<ref name=sciencemag /> ''Vaccines'' eventually decided to retract the article.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.3390/vaccines9070729 | title = Retraction: Walach et al. The Safety of COVID-19 Vaccinations—We Should Rethink the Policy | journal = Vaccines | date = 2021 | volume = 9 | issue = 7 | page = 729 | author = Vaccines Editorial Office | pmid = 34232371 | pmc = 8262594 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Cara|first=Ed|date=2 July 2017|title=Journal Retracts Terrible Study That Claimed Widespread Covid-19 Vaccine Deaths|url=https://gizmodo.com/journal-retracts-terrible-study-that-claimed-widespread-1847219596|access-date=5 July 2021|website=[[Gizmodo]]|language=en-us}}</ref>

===Stealth corrections===
A 2025 study in ''Learned Publishing'' examining journals conducting post-publication changes without indicating the permanent or temporary alterations of published material found evidence of MDPI journals engaging in this practice.<ref name="auto">{{Cite journal|title=The Existence of Stealth Corrections in Scientific Literature—A Threat to Scientific Integrity|first1=René|last1=Aquarius|first2=Floris|last2=Schoeters|first3=Nick|last3=Wise|first4=Alex|last4=Glynn|first5=Guillaume|last5=Cabanac|date=23 February 2025|journal=Learned Publishing|volume=38|issue=2|article-number=e1660|doi=10.1002/leap.1660 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2409.06852}}</ref> The study suggested that this practice may "threaten scientific integrity" as such stealth corrections may "potentially benefit journals, publishers and authors engaging in misconduct".<ref name="auto"/> The study highlighted shortcomings in MDPI editorial practices and guidelines which perpetuate this issue.<ref name="auto"/>

==Proliferation of special issues==
Paolo Crosetto, research director at [[Institut national de la recherche agronomique|INRAE]]-[[Grenoble Applied Economics Laboratory|GAEL]], first noted the proliferation of MDPI special issues in his blog in April 2021, giving them, alongside a fast turnaround time, credit for MDPI's success.<ref name=":5" /> He reported that in 2013, MDPI  published 388 special issues, or about 5 per journal, while in 2021, the number grew to nearly 40,000, or about 500 per journal.<ref name=":5" />

Special issues usually are proposed by scientists to a journal, which then makes the decision of whether or not the special issue is suitable for the journal. Crosetto noted that in contrast, "at MDPI, it is the ''publisher'' who sends out invitations for Special Issue {{Sic}}, and it is unclear which role, if any, the editorial board of the normal issues has in the process."<ref name=":5" />

In July 2021, Oviedo-García analysed the number of special issues published by MDPI journals in 2019 and 2020. In 2019, the numbers varied greatly, from 14 in the journal ''[[Vaccines (journal)|Vaccines]]'', to 500 in the journal ''[[International Journal of Molecular Sciences]]'', with the average number of special issues in each journal being 113.<ref name=Oviedo-García/> The number of special issues was more than double the number of regular issues in over 90% of MDPI journals.<ref name=Oviedo-García/> In 2020, the numbers were even higher, reaching "as surprisingly high as 788 special issues in ''[[Sustainability (journal)|Sustainability]]'', 830 in ''[[Applied Sciences (journal)|Applied Sciences]]'', and 846 in ''[[Materials (journal)|Materials]]''."<ref name=Oviedo-García/> Nearly 95% of all MDPI journals published more than one special issue per week.<ref name=Oviedo-García/>

According to Jack Grove in ''[[Inside Higher Ed]]'', ''[[International Journal of Molecular Sciences]]'' will host 3,514 "special issues with a closing date in 2023", and ''Sustainability'' 3,512, averaging over more than nine special issues per day.<ref name=Grove>{{cite journal |date=March 15, 2023 |last1=Grove |first1=Jack |title=3,514 Special Issues a Year? |journal=Inside Higher Ed |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2023/03/16/swiss-journal-publisher-raises-eyebrows-special-issues |language=en}}</ref>  This number of special issues leads to "concerns about how peer review can be conducted effectively at this scale" as well as questions about the thematic relevance to the journal.<ref name=Grove/>
